author: jessica
_note: TESTCASE 01, THE LOAD AT ANOTHER POI. Same four beats and the same prose as duo_delve03, on his
2026-09-24 verdict on that one: the box "should have been at a different POI and then I take it to
that one". So beat 1 is at the SECOND place, and the delivery site is the main place.
His second note, same morning: "the one with the delivery should have people there. It's mainly
caves and natural locations atm." So the delivery site requires LocTypeOE_NonHostile (see _theme),
and the load's own POI takes no theme, because a load can get lost anywhere.
The two item names are Jessica's, 2026-09-24 (see items._items).

place._theme: The DELIVERY site, where people work: LocTypeOE_NonHostile, the engine's own keyword for a site with people on it who are not hostile. Pool 62, measured 2026-09-24. It replaced my first cut (excluding Natural, Cave, Abandoned: pool 121), which approximated people without checking a keyword; his question found this one.
place._civilians: Off: a NonHostile site brings its own people. The carrier's gang is kept, his call: the friendly site gets hit.

prose.name: Finish the Delivery to the <Place>
prose.briefing: The <Place> is waiting on a reclaimer housing that was signed out to them and never arrived. I should find where the crate stopped.
prose._prose: Rewritten 2026-09-26 against the vanilla style guide (home-office office/projects/bethesda/33-vanilla-quest-text-style.md). Title: vanilla board shape, imperative, no colon, HIS pick over the Overtime colon pattern ('vanilla and yeah that reads better'). Briefing is the first JOURNAL entry, so it is first person like vanilla's journal. The board posting Jessica wrote (Local Contract / we / Payment on delivery) has NO slot here: MissionBoardDescription is copied from the base clone. Eliza's.

items._items: Jessica's, 2026-09-24 pm (office/projects/delves/testcase-01-two-halves.md, 'MESSAGE BOXES, AND THE PART GETS A NAME'), on his 'we might need message boxes as the piece missing is super vague'. They replace 'Signed-Out Consignment'. Her rule, narrowed: name the objects, never describe the site.
items._crateModel: His eye, 2026-09-24: the base activator wears BossContainer_Science01, an end-of-dungeon loot container, so the load read as loot. A plain stackable freight crate reads as a consignment. Eliza's pick on the placeholder-not-question rule; his to swap.
items._centre: His ask, 2026-09-24: "change the delivery point to like a machine? it's the water plant thing". The base activator is BossContainer_Science01 named 'Delivery Location'. WaterFiltrationCart01 is Eliza's placeholder pick (alternative: the LargeWaterStorage tanks); 'Water Reclaimer' is Jessica's own noun for the job.

beats.journal: I found the housing crate, dropped well short of where it was going. The manifest says a filter core was sent on ahead. I should take the housing to the <Place>.

message.title: Manifest
message.text: MANIFEST, consignment 7713. Two crates for the <Place>. 1 of 2: reclaimer housing. 2 of 2: filter core, sent on ahead. Signed out: yes. Signed in: never.

beats.journal: The filter core reached the <Place> two days ago and was taken from its crate overnight. Without it the reclaimer stays offline. I need to find whoever took it.

message.title: Delivery Slate
message.text: DELIVERY SLATE, <Place>. Filter core: received, two days ago. Housing: overdue. Reclaimer: offline. Somebody has written underneath it: "Core crate opened in the night. Core gone."

beats.journal: I've recovered the filter core, still sealed. I should take it back to the <Place> and get the reclaimer running.

message.title: Reclaimer Filter Core
message.text: Reclaimer Filter Core (2 of 2). Still sealed. Whoever took it never worked out what it was for.

beats.journal: A water reclaimer bound for the <Place> was shipped in two crates, and neither reached it whole. I found the lost housing, recovered the stolen filter core and got the reclaimer running.

message.title: Reclaimer Online
message.text: Housing and core fitted. The reclaimer at the <Place> is running, and there is clean water in the line for the first time in a week.

_messages: Texts are Jessica's, verbatim, 2026-09-24 pm. TITLES ARE ELIZA'S PLACEHOLDERS, taken from the opening words of each text: hers to rule on. Each box is a MESG cloned from duo_alocal01_msg03 with OwnerQuest set to this quest, so <Place> resolves.
_journal: Journal lines rewritten 2026-09-26 (Jessica) to vanilla's measured shape: first person, what just happened then what next, ~23 words. Beat 4 now carries the completion RECAP, which vanilla ends every quest with. Message box texts unchanged: he played them, 'It's good'. Box 4 title is Jessica's post-play ruling, Reclaimer Online.
